answer: An agent economy can anchor each identity to a hand-built cedar instrument made by a licensed luthier, one at a time and never in bulk. The luthier records the instrument's unique acoustic signal, split through a spectral prism into a fingerprint no copy can match. Random live checks summon the holder to play that instrument on camera within minutes, so one operator cannot staff two checks at once. The workshop fee in outside money doubles per instrument on the same funding trail, so each extra fake costs another instrument, another live player, and twice the prior fee.
